fig-deployment-mask.ariaDescription: A row of deployment steps on the left maps by index into bit positions in a uint256 mask on the right. Each step sets its bit only when code exists at that configured address.
fig-deployment-mask.ariaLabel: Deployment mask maps ordered deployment steps to bits

fig-invariant-layers.ariaDescription:
Four connected layers run from local authority guards through
							cross-contract conservation and lifecycle liveness to economic
							security. A failure in an earlier layer invalidates the safety
							claims built above it.

children.text: Each layer depends on every invariant to its left.

fig-liquidation-punitive-flow.ariaDescription: Liquidation moves only fully funded coverage commitment and its complete 5%-bonus pool-held vault REP backing award. Escalation claims, fees, and all surplus remain with the target; a maximum request records untransferred residual coverage commitment as bad debt.
fig-liquidation-punitive-flow.ariaLabel: Liquidation moves funded coverage commitment and its pool-held vault REP backing award while target claims, fees, and surplus remain behind and residual coverage commitment becomes bad debt.

children.text: receives pool-held vault REP backing award

fig-mmr-peaks.ariaDescription: A leaf count of thirteen is shown as binary one one zero one, corresponding to occupied peaks at heights zero, two, and three which are later bagged into one root.
fig-mmr-peaks.ariaLabel: Merkle Mountain Range peaks are determined by set bits in the leaf count

fig-mmr-proof-anatomy.ariaDescription: The membership lane combines the carried deposit leaf with bottom-up siblings inside its selected peak, then with other occupied peak roots in ascending height order to reconstruct the snapshot root. The nullifier lane hashes the stable parent deposit index and combines it with a fixed-depth sibling path to prove the claim has not already been consumed.
fig-mmr-proof-anatomy.ariaLabel: A carried-deposit proof has an MMR membership lane and a separate nullifier lane

fig-openoracle-integration-flow.ariaDescription:
Statoblast queues solvency-sensitive operations behind a bounded
							OpenOracle REP/ETH report and executes them only with a fresh
							accepted price.

children.text: fresh price, pending report, and local safety checks
Expired operations, stale liquidations, zero-effect withdrawals,

fig-statoblast-pool-accounting.ariaDescription:
REP deposits mint proportional REP backing units, decayed
								settlement collateral increments the fee index, and vault coverage commitments claim
								fees from that index.

fig-statoblast-share-lifecycle.ariaDescription:
ETH mints Invalid, Yes, and No shares. Operational pools redeem
								full sets, and finalized winning shares redeem through outcome
								settlement.

fig-statoblast-share-migration.ariaDescription:
On first materialization into untouched children, the full current
								parent balance materializes in each selected child token id while
								the source remains locked as an entitlement. Later calls mint only
								the unmaterialized delta for each child.
fig-statoblast-share-migration.ariaLabel: Share migration materializes persistent branch entitlements

fig-statoblast-escalation-cost-curve.ariaDescription: Cumulative binding capital rises exponentially from the normalized starting bond to one hundred percent of the non-decision threshold over the full escalation interval; individual deposits retain the fixed start-bond minimum.
fig-statoblast-escalation-cost-curve.ariaLabel: Exponential cumulative binding-capital threshold from the starting bond to the non-decision threshold

fig-statoblast-fork-state-machine.ariaDescription:
Contract states and conditional transition functions from an
								operational parent through migration and bounded truth-auction
								settlement to an operational child.

children.text: immediate if no auction is needed

fig-statoblast-system-decision-flow.ariaDescription:
Question, pool, escalation, fork, child migration, auction
								repair, fixed-outcome settlement, and unresolved recursive
								continuation flow.

fig-statoblast-auction-balance-sheet.ariaDescription:
A child pool before auction, after full auction repair, and after
								weak auction demand settles at the collateral actually raised.

fig-statoblast-oracle-flow.ariaDescription:
A solvency-sensitive operation either executes immediately with
								a valid cached price or stages behind a pending OpenOracle
								report.

fig-auction-lifecycle.ariaDescription:
Auction Lifecycle
					After migration closes, startTruthAuction takes one of two paths. When no sale is required, TruthAuctionFinalized activates the child immediately and bypasses AuctionStarted, bidding, and bid settlement. Otherwise AuctionStarted opens bidding; finalizeTruthAuction later computes clearing and activates the child, and paged calls then settle individual claims and refunds.
fig-auction-lifecycle.ariaLabel: After migration closes, startTruthAuction either finalizes the child immediately without bids or starts an auction whose later finalization activates the child before individual bids settle.

fig-auction-clearing-ladder.ariaDescription: High-price bids are considered first. If cumulative demand reaches the ETH raise cap or REP sale cap, the first binding tick sets normal uniform clearing. If neither cap is reached, finalization selects bids at or above the cap-implied qualification tick and allocates the complete REP sale cap among them at one effective price. With no qualifying bids, every bid refunds.
fig-auction-clearing-ladder.ariaLabel: Auction demand is evaluated from high ticks to low ticks before uniform or underfunded clearing

children.text: first ETH or REP cap reached
complete REP cap shared pro rata

fig-zoltar-fork-branch-set.ariaDescription: Universe tree. A fork creates the full valid branch set; no branch is privileged by the contract.
fig-zoltar-fork-branch-set.ariaLabel: A parent universe forks into children for Invalid and each valid outcome.

fig-zoltar-threshold-deposit.ariaDescription: Threshold Deposit Split. The full parent-REP threshold leaves parent supply. Most is re-expressed as migratable child-REP credit; the haircut is not credited.
fig-zoltar-threshold-deposit.ariaLabel: Fork threshold deposit leaves the parent universe. After flooring the approximately 20 percent uncredited haircut, the remainder is an approximately 80 percent migration balance.

children.text: Fork initiator deposits the attoREP-denominated fork threshold

fig-zoltar-packed-scalar-answer.ariaDescription: Packed Scalar Answer. A scalar answer is easier to read as reserved bits, a namespace flag, and two payout fields: bits 254...240 must be zero, 0 in bit 255 is the invalid namespace, and 1 means the payout fields must sum to numTicks.
fig-zoltar-packed-scalar-answer.ariaLabel: A uint256 scalar answer uses the highest bit as a namespace flag, then packs first and second 120-bit payout numerators.

children.text: Bits 254...240 are reserved and must be zero.

fig-contract-interaction-map.ariaDescription: Three panels separate construction-time deployment, recurring market and oracle operations, and fork migration and backing repair. Repeated contracts preserve local reading order, short edge labels name each action, and the detailed table below gives the exact boundary.
fig-contract-interaction-map.ariaLabel: Zoltar and Statoblast contract interactions grouped into deployment, runtime, and fork phases

fig-statoblast-retention-utilization.ariaDescription: The annualized open-interest fee rises from about ten percent at zero utilization to about fifty percent at the eighty-percent utilization dip, then remains at that level as the per-second retention rate stays at its minimum.
fig-statoblast-retention-utilization.ariaLabel: Annualized open-interest fee across fee-eligible coverage commitment utilization

fig-zoltar-fork-threshold-decay.ariaDescription: With the default threshold and burn divisors, each fork haircut leaves approximately ninety-nine percent of the previous generation's theoretical REP supply. The next fork threshold remains five percent of that declining supply.
fig-zoltar-fork-threshold-decay.ariaLabel: Theoretical REP supply and fork threshold across repeated forks
